_what: How several tool calls are made together so that the whole either stands or is put back (tool-transaction.mjs, the MCP tool run_tools_together). A plan is steps; each step has an id, a tool and its input, and any value in an input may be `{ "$from": "<step id>.result.<path>" }` to take it from an earlier step (a path is keys separated by dots, `[*]` collects a field from every item of a list). There is no code in a plan: nothing is evaluated, so there is nothing to escape from. If a step fails, every step already done is put back in reverse order. A step can be put back when its tool only reads (`read_only_tools` are found from the tool's own hint), when its result carries the call that undoes it (`reverse_result_fields`), or when `reversals` has a row for its tool (a row with `undo` names the call and where its input comes from; a row with `by_result` says the result carries the call); any other step can only be the LAST step, because nothing after it could be undone. `failed_when` says what in a result counts as a failure even when the call did not throw. `limits` bound a plan. Adding a reversible tool is one row. `tool_name` is the MCP tool that runs a plan.

errors.NOT_A_PLAN: steps must be a list of { id, tool, input }.
errors.TOO_MANY_STEPS: A plan holds at most {most} steps.
errors.BAD_STEP: Step {index} needs an id, a tool name and (optionally) an input object.
errors.UNKNOWN_TOOL: Step "{id}" names the tool "{tool}", which does not exist.
errors.NESTED: Step "{id}" is itself a plan; plans do not nest.
errors.CANNOT_BE_PUT_BACK: Step "{id}" ({tool}) cannot be put back and is not the last step, so a later failure could not be undone. Move it last, or leave it out.
errors.BAD_REFERENCE: Step "{id}" reads from "{from}", which is not an earlier step's result.
errors.REFERENCE_UNRESOLVED: Step "{id}" reads "{from}", which the earlier result does not hold.
